title: Safety and Efficacy of the BNT162b2 mRNA Covid-19 Vaccine
authors: Polack FP; Thomas SJ; Kitchin N
abstract: A two-dose regimen of BNT162b2 conferred 95% protection against Covid-19 in persons 16 years of age or older. Safety over a median of 2 months was similar to that of other viral vaccines.
keywords: BNT162b2; mRNA; efficacy; safety; clinical trial

title: Efficacy and Safety of the mRNA-1273 SARS-CoV-2 Vaccine
authors: Baden LR; El Sahly HM; Essink B
abstract: The mRNA-1273 vaccine showed 94.1% efficacy at preventing Covid-19 illness, including severe disease. Aside from transient local and systemic reactions, no safety concerns were identified.
keywords: mRNA-1273; Moderna; efficacy; lipid nanoparticle; phase 3

title: Safety and efficacy of the ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 vaccine (AZD1222) against SARS-CoV-2
authors: Voysey M; Clemens SAC; Madhi SA
abstract: ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 has an acceptable safety profile and has been found to be efficacious against symptomatic COVID-19 in this interim analysis of ongoing clinical trials with 70.4% overall efficacy.
keywords: ChAdOx1; AstraZeneca; viral vector; efficacy; safety

title: Safety and efficacy of an rAd26 and rAd5 vector-based heterologous prime-boost COVID-19 vaccine
authors: Logunov DY; Dolzhikova IV; Shcheblyakov DV
abstract: Interim analysis of the phase 3 trial of Gam-COVID-Vac showed 91.6% efficacy against COVID-19 and was well tolerated in a large cohort.

title: BNT162b2 mRNA Covid-19 Vaccine in a Nationwide Mass Vaccination Setting
authors: Dagan N; Barda N; Kepten E
abstract: Estimated vaccine effectiveness for documented infection was 92% and for symptomatic illness was 94% after two doses in a real-world nationwide mass vaccination campaign.

title: Safety and Efficacy of Single-Dose Ad26.COV2.S Vaccine against Covid-19
authors: Sadoff J; Gray G; Vandebosch A
abstract: Single-dose Ad26.COV2.S protected against symptomatic Covid-19 with 66.9% efficacy against moderate to severe-critical disease and higher efficacy against severe hospitalization.

title: Effectiveness of Covid-19 Vaccines against the B.1.617.2 (Delta) Variant
authors: Lopez Bernal J; Andrews N; Gower C
abstract: Effectiveness after two doses of BNT162b2 was 88.0% against the delta variant and 67.0% with two doses of ChAdOx1 nCoV-19.
keywords: Delta variant; B.1.617.2; vaccine effectiveness; BNT162b2; ChAdOx1

title: Reports of Anaphylaxis After Receipt of mRNA COVID-19 Vaccines in the US
authors: Shimabukuro TT; Cole M; Su JR
abstract: Analysis of VAERS monitoring data found anaphylaxis following mRNA COVID-19 vaccination to be a rare adverse event (4.7 cases per million doses for Pfizer-BioNTech and 2.5 for Moderna).
keywords: VAERS; anaphylaxis; adverse events; mRNA safety

title: Thrombotic Thrombocytopenia after ChAdOx1 nCov-19 Vaccination
authors: Greinacher A; Thiele T; Warkentin TE
abstract: Rare immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia mediated by platelet-activating antibodies against PF4 was observed following ChAdOx1 nCov-19 vaccination.
keywords: VITT; thrombocytopenia; AstraZeneca; adverse events; safety

title: Waning Immunity after the BNT162b2 Vaccine in Israel
authors: Goldberg Y; Mandel M; Bar-On YM
abstract: Immunity against the delta variant of SARS-CoV-2 waned in all age groups a few months after receipt of the second dose of vaccine, supporting booster evaluation.
keywords: waning immunity; booster; BNT162b2; delta variant

title: Efficacy, safety, and lot-to-lot immunogenicity of an inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine (BBV152)
authors: Ella R; Reddy S; Blackwelder W
abstract: BBV152 (Covaxin) demonstrated 77.8% overall efficacy against symptomatic COVID-19 in a phase 3 double-blind randomized controlled trial in India.
keywords: BBV152; Covaxin; inactivated vaccine; efficacy; phase 3
